title: Jacobi-symbol invariant
statement: For Boolean words $z$ and $S$, the invariant holds if there exist Boolean words $A,N,s$ such that $S$ encodes $A$ paired with $N$ paired with $s$, the lengths of $A$ and $N$ are each at most the length of $z$, and $s$ has length at most one. Moreover, if the value of the second component decoded from $z$ is odd, then the value of $N$ is odd and the sign of $s$ times the Jacobi symbol of the values of $A$ and $N$ equals the Jacobi symbol of the values of the two components decoded from $z$.
caveat: The pair encoding, component decoders, Boolean-word value convention, and sign convention are not defined in the supplied statement.
